details:
So I have been with vrchat 100% since getting my headset in January. 
And yhe first thing I loved was the community and how driven every individual was and remains to push others and get them all to greatness. And those that attain that stature remember who put them there and do give to the community. This isn't a game it is a social setting and place for communication between people. And it's that communication and sharing that gets worlds recognixed,  content creators verified and loved and much much more.

Now currently I know the company side of things can't take sides and prefer certain people over others and also they can't help promote monetary things that support the community. That's understandable that they can't take sides

However this does leave the community to go a bit rampant. Thankfully it's the care and compassion for the platform that has kept it from collapsing. However I see parts where it may collapse in particular to twitch and lewds

There is a recent trend of lewd avatars with barely any clothing and almost as a test to see how much of a naked woman can be exposed and not exposed before the devs do anything. 
I have kids in my vr family,  I have kids in my streams some times. Now I know vrchat and vr isn't for kids and they are aware of the risks.  But those risks are avoided by going to the right worlds and seeing the right people.  But you go in to a public, chances are you'll be lewded by a ricardo or have a tattooed nipple in your eye.

I suggest a seperate tag on world's and nametags that has a vrchat verified SFW and NSFW tag. (Similar to twitters verification system) So people are aware of certain avatars and world's and can seperately choose to not see them (added feature in the safety settings). 

This way people can protect themselves and others but also doesn't flat out destroy the NSFW stuff in terms of some avatars, social media profiles and fan art within the community (cause come on, sex sells and we're all entitled to our own lovely bodies) 

This is not to destroy the NSFW. Bit to seperate it and avoid the community becoming too lewd and twitch bringing the hammer down
title: Community observations
